          "answer": "# Wudu and Its Requirement Before Salah\n\n## General Requirement\n\nBased on the evidence provided, wudu (ritual ablution) is indeed among the **required conditions** that must be fulfilled for salah (prayer) to be valid. This is clearly implied in the rulings, which treat wudu as a prerequisite alongside other conditions such as having pure clothing and facing the qibla [1].\n\n## Wudu as a Condition of Prayer\n\nThe requirement of wudu is treated as an ongoing condition during prayer, not merely something required at the outset. If a condition such as the validity of one's wudu is **invalidated during the prayer** — for example, by passing urine — the prayer itself becomes invalid [2]. This demonstrates that maintaining ritual purity through wudu is integral to the validity of salah throughout its performance.\n\n## When Tayammum Substitutes for Wudu\n\nIn circumstances where wudu cannot be performed (e.g., shortage of time or inability to use water), **tayammum** may serve as a substitute. If a person performs tayammum in place of *ghusl for janabah*, no additional wudu is required for prayer [5]. However, for tayammum performed in place of other types of ghusl (excluding the ghusl for medium istihādah), it is **recommended as a precaution** to also perform wudu, or if that is not possible, to perform a separate tayammum in its place [5].\n\n## Wudu Must Be Performed With Proper Intention\n\nFor wudu to be valid and thus qualify as a prerequisite for salah, it **must be performed with the intention of attaining proximity to Allah (qasd al-qurbah)**. If someone performs wudu merely to cool down or for another worldly purpose, it is considered **invalid** [3].\n\n## Wudu as a Condition for Make-Up Acts\n\nThe requirement of wudu extends beyond the prayer itself. For example, if a person forgets a *sajdah* and must make it up after the prayer, they must do so while fulfilling **all the conditions of prayer**, which implicitly includes being in a state of ritual purity [4].\n\n---\n\nIn summary, wudu is a **fundamental prerequisite** for the validity of salah, must be maintained throughout the prayer, and must be performed with the correct intention. It may only be replaced by tayammum under specific valid circumstances [1][2][3][5].\n## Sources\n[1] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER TWO, 8. rubbing oil on the body;, Ruling 461.0\n[2] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER THREE, 6. Translation of the complete tashahhud and salām, Ruling 1112.0\n[3] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER TWO, 12. Flowing out of blood [of a slaughtered animal] in a normal quantity, Ruling 280.0\n[4] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER THREE, 2. one inadvertently talks during prayers;, Ruling 1237.0\n[5] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER TWO, 7. Shortage of time, Ruling 712.0\n\n---\nNote: This is based on Ayatollah Sistani's published rulings. For a definitive ruling, consult a qualified jurist or Sistani's official office.",

          "answer": "## Does Sleep Break Wudu?\n\nYes, **sleep breaks wudu** according to Ayatollah Sistani's rulings.\n\nRuling 322 explicitly lists the seven things that invalidate wudu, and **sleep is the fourth item** on this list [11]. However, the ruling provides an important clarification regarding what constitutes sleep in this context:\n\n> *\"Sleeping, which means that simultaneously one's eyes do not see and one's ears do not hear; however, if one's eyes do not see but his ears hear, his wuḍūʾ does not become invalid.\"* [11]\n\n### Key Points:\n\n- **Full sleep** (where both sight and hearing are lost simultaneously) **invalidates wudu** [11].\n- **Partial sleep** (where the eyes may be closed but the ears can still hear) **does not invalidate wudu** [11].\n- Sleep is treated consistently as a nullifier of wudu in other rulings as well — for example, a person with a medical condition affecting bladder/bowel control would need to renew their wudu if they slept between prayers [17].\n- Since tayammum performed in place of wudu is invalidated by the same things that invalidate wudu, **sleep would also invalidate a tayammum** performed as a substitute for wudu [7].\n\nIn summary, if you fall into a sleep deep enough that you can neither see nor hear, your wudu is broken and you will need to perform a new wudu before acts that require it.\n## Sources\n[7] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER TWO, 7. Shortage of time, Ruling 709.0\n[11] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER TWO, 6. istiḥāḍah of a woman, which will be discussed later;, Ruling 322.0\n[17] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER TWO, 12. Flowing out of blood [of a slaughtered animal] in a normal quantity, Ruling 307.0\n\n---\nNote: This is based on Ayatollah Sistani's published rulings.           "answer": "## Ruling on Eating Shrimp\n\nThe evidence provided does not contain a direct ruling on shrimp specifically. However, the relevant principle that governs sea creatures in Ayatollah Sistani's rulings concerns **whether a fish has scales**, which is the key criterion for determining the permissibility of eating sea creatures.\n\n### The Core Rule for Sea Creatures\n\nAccording to the rulings, fish that are **commonly considered to have scales** are lawful to eat, provided they are caught alive and die out of the water (or die in a fishing net in the water) [1]. Conversely, **fish that are commonly considered not to have scales are unlawful to eat**, even if caught alive and dying out of the water [1].\n\n### Applying This to Shrimp\n\nShrimp do **not** have scales — they have a hard outer shell (exoskeleton). Based on the principle established in Ruling 2632, animals that are commonly considered not to have scales are **unlawful to eat** [1].\n\n### Important Caveat\n\nThe evidence provided here does not include an **explicit, direct ruling on shrimp** by name.           "usage_present": true,
          "answer_chars": 4626,
          "answer": "# When Khums Becomes Due on Savings\n\n## The Basic Principle\n\nKhums is obligatory on **surplus income** — that is, the amount remaining after deducting your annual living expenses from your earnings [4]. Here is a breakdown of the key rules:\n\n---\n\n## Who Must Pay and When\n\n### People with a Regular Occupation\nIf you are a businessman, merchant, craftsman, clerk, or similar worker, you must pay khums on whatever **exceeds your living expenses after one full year** has passed from the start of your khums year [1]. The same applies to preachers and others whose income may arrive at irregular intervals, as long as it covers a significant portion of their yearly living expenses [1].\n\n### People Without a Regular Occupation\nIf you do not have a regular occupation and receive assistance from the government or others, or if you occasionally receive a windfall profit, you must still pay khums on whatever exceeds your yearly living expenses **after one year has passed from the time you received that income**. In this case, you may calculate a separate khums year for each individual amount received [1].\n\n---\n\n## What Can Be Deducted Before Calculating Khums\n\n- **Living expenses** for the year may be deducted from your profit [1].\n- **Business-related costs** such as brokerage fees, transportation costs, and wear and tear on tools and equipment may also be deducted [3].\n- If you have **multiple lines of business** that share the same bookkeeping and profit/loss accounts, losses may be offset against gains. However, if two lines of business are separate, losses from one generally cannot offset profits from the other [7].\n- If you own **other property on which khums is not obligatory**, you may calculate your living expenses solely from your earned profit [6].\n\n---\n\n## Household Items and Purchases During the Year\n\nIf you purchase household items from your profit during the year and use them before the khums year ends, those items are **not liable for khums**, provided they were needed. Items typically stored for future seasonal use (e.g., winter or summer clothing) are also exempt even if unused during the year [8].\n\n---\n\n## Borrowing and Loans\n\nIf you borrow money **during the year to cover living expenses** and then earn a profit before the year ends, the borrowed amount may be deducted from that profit [2]. However, if a year ends without profit and you had borrowed money for living expenses, you **cannot deduct that amount from future years' profits** to reduce khums liability [2].\n\n---\n\n## Important Deadline\n\nOnce your property becomes liable for khums and a year has passed, you **do not have rightful disposal over that portion** of your property until khums is paid [9].\n\n---\n\n## Special Cases\n\n- Property received as **khums or zakat** by an eligible recipient is not itself liable for khums, but any profit earned *from* it that exceeds yearly living expenses is liable [10].\n- Property acquired from **someone who does not pay khums** (e.g., a disbeliever) is not obligatory to pay khums on [12].\n- If a person **dies during the khums year**, living expenses up to the time of death are deducted from the profit, and khums on the remainder must be paid immediately [5].\n\n---\n\nIn summary, khums on savings is due **once a full year has passed** and you have income remaining **above and beyond your reasonable living expenses** for that year [1].\n## Sources\n[1] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER SIX, 1.           "usage_present": true,
          "answer_chars": 2491,
          "answer": "# Fasting While Travelling\n\nThe permissibility of fasting while travelling depends on several key factors according to Ayatollah Sistani's rulings:\n\n## General Rule: Fasting is Invalid While Travelling\n\nA traveller **must not fast** if his obligation during travel is to shorten his prayers (perform them in *qaṣr* form, i.e., four-unit prayers shortened to two units) [2]. This is the default ruling for most travellers.\n\n## Exceptions: When Fasting IS Required or Valid While Travelling\n\n1. **Travellers who pray in full (*tamām*)**: A traveller who is required to perform his prayers in their complete form — such as a person whose **occupation involves travelling** or whose **journey is sinful** — must fast on his journey [2].\n\n2. **Intending to stay for ten days**: A traveller who makes the intention to remain in a place for ten days **must keep obligatory fasts** and may also keep recommended fasts [5].\n\n3. **Vows made specifically for travel days**: If a person makes a vow to fast on a particular day while travelling, or vows to fast on a specific day whether travelling or not, he must fulfil that fast even while travelling [4].\n\n## Important Notes on Ignorance of the Ruling\n\n- If someone **does not know** that a traveller's fast is invalid and fasts on a journey, his fast becomes invalid upon learning the ruling during the day. However, if he does not find out until *maghrib*, his fast is considered valid [3].\n- If a person **forgets** he is travelling, or forgets that a traveller's fast is invalid, his fast is considered invalid based on obligatory precaution [1].\n\n## Summary\n\nIn most cases, fasting while travelling is **not valid** and must be made up later. However, exceptions exist for those who pray in full during travel, those intending a ten-day stay, and those bound by specific vows [2][5][4].\n## Sources\n[1] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER FOUR, 11. immersing the entire head in water., Ruling 1689.0\n[2] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER FOUR, 11. immersing the entire head in water., Ruling 1683.0\n[3] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER FOUR, 11. immersing the entire head in water., Ruling 1688.0\n[4] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER FOUR, 11. immersing the entire head in water., Ruling 1686.0\n[5] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER THREE, 2. one inadvertently talks during prayers;, Ruling 1333.0\n\n---\nNote: This is based on Ayatollah Sistani's published rulings. For a definitive ruling, consult a qualified jurist or Sistani's official office.",

          "usage_present": true,
          "answer_chars": 2014,
          "answer": "## Ghusl After a Wet Dream\n\nBased on the available evidence, here is what Ayatollah Sistani's rulings state regarding ghusl after a wet dream:\n\n### Ghusl is Required, But Not Always Immediately\n\nA wet dream results in the state of **janābah** (major ritual impurity), which necessitates **ghusl al-janābah**. The rulings indicate that ghusl for janābah can be performed in two ways: the **sequential (tartībī)** method or the **immersive (irtimāsī)** method [3].\n\n### Timing of Ghusl\n\nImportantly, the ghusl does not always have to be performed immediately. Specifically:\n\n- If a person who is **fasting** has a wet dream during the day, **it is not obligatory to perform ghusl immediately** [1]. This indicates there is some flexibility in the timing of the ghusl.\n\n### Practical Recommendation Before Performing Ghusl\n\nIf a fasting person has had a wet dream and suspects that semen may still remain in the penis, the **recommended precaution** is to **urinate before performing ghusl**, so that any remaining semen is expelled beforehand and does not discharge after the ghusl has been completed [4].\n\n### Effect on Fasting\n\nIt should also be noted that if a person wakes up **after the time of Ṣubḥ prayers** in Ramadan and discovers they had a wet dream — even if the wet dream occurred before Ṣubḥ — their **fast remains valid** [5].\n\n---\n\nIn summary, ghusl **is required** following a wet dream due to the resulting state of janābah [3], though it need not necessarily be performed immediately in all circumstances [1].\n## Sources\n[1] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER FOUR, 8. Vomiting, Ruling 1603.0\n[3] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER TWO, 8. rubbing oil on the body;, Ruling 359.0\n[4] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER FOUR, 5. Causing thick dust to reach the throat, Ruling 1572.0\n[5] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER FOUR, 8. Vomiting, Ruling 1604.0\n\n---\nNote: This is based on Ayatollah Sistani's published rulings.           "usage_present": true,
          "answer_chars": 2571,
          "answer": "## Praying with Wet Socks and Removing Rings for Wudu\n\n### 1. Praying with Wet (or Impure) Socks\n\nRegarding socks during prayer, the relevant ruling addresses the case of **small items of clothing that cannot cover the private parts** (such as socks):\n\n- If socks become **impure (najis)**, prayers performed while wearing them are still **valid**, provided the socks are not made from an impure carcass or an intrinsically impure animal (such as a dog) [3].\n- If the socks *are* made from such materials (impure carcass or an impure animal), then **based on obligatory precaution, prayers are invalid** when wearing them [3].\n\nSo, if your socks are simply **wet** (with water, for example) but not ritually impure, there is no issue with praying in them. Even if they were impure in the standard sense, the prayer would remain valid as long as they don't fall into the exceptional categories mentioned above [3].\n\n---\n\n### 2. Removing Rings for Wudu\n\nYes, **rings must be removed** during wudu. Specifically:\n\n- One **must remove any rings from his fingers when wiping over his hands** during wudu [2].\n- More broadly, if there is any obstruction on the forehead, back of the hands, or palms — such as something stuck to them — it must also be removed to ensure water reaches the skin properly [2].\n\n#### Note on Rings During Prayer Itself:\n- For **men**, wearing a **gold ring** is unlawful, and performing prayers while wearing one renders the prayer **invalid** [1].\n- For **women**, wearing gold (including rings) during prayer is **not a problem** [1].\n- An **impure ring** (regardless of material), however, does **not** invalidate the prayer — there is explicitly no problem in praying with an impure ring [3].\n\n---\n\n### Summary Table\n\n| Scenario | Ruling |\n|---|---|\n| Praying with wet/impure socks (normal material) | Valid [3] |\n| Praying with socks from impure carcass/animal | Invalid (obligatory precaution) [3] |\n| Removing rings for wudu | Required [2] |\n| Men praying with a gold ring | Invalid [1] |\n| Women praying with a gold ring | Permissible [1] |\n| Praying with an impure ring | Valid [3] |\n## Sources\n[1] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER THREE, 1. it must be pure (ṭāhir);, Ruling 819.0\n[2] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER TWO, 7.           "usage_present": true,
          "answer_chars": 5512,
          "answer": "# Rulings on Fasting When Ill, Travelling, or Pregnant\n\n## 1. Illness\n\n**When fasting is not obligatory:**\nIf fasting would cause significant harm due to illness, a person is not obliged to fast. Importantly, this is determined by the person's own reasonable assessment — someone who is **certain or supposes** that fasting will cause them significant harm is not obliged to fast, even if a doctor says otherwise. Conversely, someone who **knows** fasting will not cause significant harm must fast, even if a doctor advises against it [10].\n\n**Making up missed fasts (Qaḍāʾ):**\n- If a person's illness is cured after Ramadan and before the following Ramadan, they **must make up** the missed fasts [6].\n- If the illness **continues until the following Ramadan**, it is **not obligatory** to make up the missed fasts. Instead, for each missed day, one *mudd* (approximately 750 grams) of food must be given to a poor person as *fidyah* [7].\n- If illness persists for **several years**, the person must make up the fasts for the **last** Ramadan once recovered, and for each missed day of the **previous years**, give one *mudd* of food to a poor person [8].\n- If illness caused missed fasts but another legitimate excuse then arose preventing make-up before the next Ramadan, the fasts must still be made up; and based on obligatory precaution, one *mudd* per missed fast should also be given [6].\n\n**Special case — severe thirst:**\nIf a person's illness causes extreme, unbearable thirst, fasting is not obligatory. If the thirst is merely excessively difficult (but bearable), fasting is still not obligatory, but one *mudd* of food per missed fast must be given; however, in this case, **make-up fasts are not required** even if he recovers [9].\n\n---\n\n## 2. Travelling\n\n**General rule:**\nA traveller who is obliged to shorten their prayers (perform them in *qaṣr* form) **must not fast** while travelling. However, a traveller who performs prayers in their complete (*tamām*) form — such as a person whose profession involves travel, or whose journey is sinful — **must fast** even while travelling [12].\n\n**Intention to stay:**\nA traveller who intends to remain in a place for **ten days** must keep obligatory fasts during that stay [14].\n\n**Ignorance of the ruling:**\n- If someone does not know that a traveller's fast is invalid and fasts while travelling, then discovers the ruling **during the day**, their fast is invalid [13].\n- If they do not discover it until *maghrib*, their fast is **valid** [13].\n- If a person **forgets** they are travelling and fasts anyway, their fast is invalid based on obligatory precaution [11].\n\n**Vows while travelling:**\nIf a person makes a vow to fast on a specific day regardless of whether they are travelling, they must fulfil that fast even on a journey [15].\n\n---\n\n## 3. Pregnancy\n\n**Pregnant women approaching delivery:**\nIf fasting would be harmful to a **pregnant woman nearing delivery** or to her **unborn child**, fasting is not obligatory. She must:\n1. Give **one *mudd* of food** to a poor person for each missed fast, and\n2. **Make up** the missed fasts afterwards [2].\n\n**Breastfeeding women** (closely related):\nIf fasting is harmful to a **breastfeeding woman** (whether the mother, a wet nurse, or an unpaid caregiver) or to the child she is nursing, fasting is not obligatory. She must likewise give one *mudd* per missed fast and make up those fasts. Based on obligatory precaution, this exemption applies only when breastfeeding is the sole means of feeding the child [1].\n\n---\n\n## Summary Table\n\n| Situation | Fasting Obligatory? | Make-Up Required? | Fidyah (per day)? |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Illness, recovers before next Ramadan | No | Yes | No (unless another excuse intervened [6]) |\n| Illness continues until next Ramadan | No | No | Yes — 1 *mudd* [7] |\n| Illness for multiple years | No | Yes (last Ramadan only) | Yes — for prior years [8] |\n| Travelling (*qaṣr* prayers) | No | Yes [7] | Obligatory precaution: Yes [7] |\n| Pregnancy (near delivery, harmful) | No | Yes | Yes — 1 *mudd* [2] |\n| Breastfeeding (harmful to mother/child) | No | Yes | Yes — 1 *mudd* [1] |\n## Sources\n[1] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER FOUR, 11. immersing the entire head in water., Ruling 1698.0\n[2] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER FOUR, 11. immersing the entire head in water., Ruling 1697.0\n[6] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER FOUR, 11. immersing the entire head in water., Ruling 1673.0\n[7] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER FOUR, 11. immersing the entire head in water., Ruling 1672.0\n[8] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER FOUR, 11. immersing the entire head in water., Ruling 1676.0\n[9] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER FOUR, 11. immersing the entire head in water., Ruling 1696.0\n[10] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER FIVE, 4. a woman whose ḥayḍ or nifās stops during the day;, Ruling 1711.0\n[11] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER FOUR, 11. immersing the entire head in water., Ruling 1689.0\n[12] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER FOUR, 11. immersing the entire head in water., Ruling 1683.0\n[13] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER FOUR, 11. immersing the entire head in water., Ruling 1688.0\n[14] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER THREE, 2. one inadvertently talks during prayers;, Ruling 1333.0\n[15] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER FOUR, 11. immersing the entire head in water., Ruling 1686.0\n\n---\nNote: This is based on Ayatollah Sistani's published rulings.           "answer_chars": 2226,
          "answer": "## Missed Prayers (Qaḍāʾ) for Fajr and Dhuhr Over Two Days\n\n### How Many Prayers Do You Owe?\n\nBased on the five obligatory daily prayers [4], you have missed the following:\n\n- **Fajr (Ṣubḥ)** — 2 missed prayers (one per day)\n- **Ẓuhr (Dhuhr)** — 2 missed prayers (one per day)\n\nThis gives you a **total of 4 qaḍāʾ prayers** to make up.\n\n---\n\n### How to Make Them Up\n\n**1. Order of Performance**\n\nIt is **not necessary** to make up these missed prayers in the exact order they originally became missed (qaḍāʾ) [1]. For example, you do not need to make up Day 1's Fajr before Day 2's Fajr, or Fajr before Ẓuhr across the two days.\n\nHowever, there is an important exception: **within the same day**, Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr prayers must be performed in their proper order when made up together, as must Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ [1]. Since you are only making up Fajr and Ẓuhr, and these two do not have a required sequence between them, you have flexibility in how you order them.\n\n**2. Performing the Prayers**\n\nEach prayer should be performed as it normally would be:\n- **Fajr (Ṣubḥ):** 2 rakʿahs [4]\n- **Ẓuhr:** 4 rakʿahs [4]\n\n**3. Precautionary Note**\n\nIf you are uncertain whether a prayer you performed was valid, it is **recommended** to make it up as a precautionary measure [5].\n\n---\n\n### Summary\n\nYou owe **4 qaḍāʾ prayers** in total, and you may perform them in any order that is convenient for you, with the flexibility that no strict sequence is required between Fajr and Ẓuhr [1]. The important thing is to perform each prayer correctly according to its prescribed number of rakʿahs [4].\n## Sources\n[1] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER THREE, 2. one inadvertently talks during prayers;, Ruling 1360.0\n[4] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER THREE, 7. Shortage of time, Ruling 715.0\n[5] Islamic Laws 4th Edition, CHAPTER THREE, 2. one inadvertently talks during prayers;, Ruling 1359.0\n\n⚠️ Insufficient Evidence: The retrieved sources do not fully address this question.           "usage_by_site": {

          "usage_totals": {

            "cache_read_input_tokens": 2322,
            "cache_creation_input_tokens": 1955
          },
          "usage_present": true,
          "answer_chars": 4452,
          "answer": "# اسلام میں صبر کی اہمیت\n\nآپ کا سوال بہت اہم اور روح پرور ہے۔ صبر اسلامی تعلیمات کے ستونوں میں سے ایک ہے، اور قرآن و اہلِ بیت (علیہم السلام) کی احادیث میں اس موضوع پر بے پناہ رہنمائی موجود ہے۔ آیئے اسے تفصیل سے سمجھتے ہیں۔\n\n---\n\n## قرآنِ کریم میں صبر\n\nاللہ تعالیٰ نے قرآنِ مجید میں تقریباً **ستّر مقامات** پر صبر کا ذکر فرمایا ہے، جو اس کی غیرمعمولی اہمیت کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔\n\nسورۂ بقرہ میں اللہ تعالیٰ فرماتا ہے:\n\n***\"اے ایمان والو! صبر اور نماز کے ذریعے (اللہ سے) مدد مانگو؛ بے شک اللہ صبر کرنے والوں کے ساتھ ہے۔\"***\n(سورۂ بقرہ، آیت ۱۵۳)\n\nعلامہ سید محمد حسین طباطبائی اپنی تفسیر **المیزان** (جلد ۲، سورۂ بقرہ، آیات ۱۵۳-۱۵۷) میں فرماتے ہیں کہ صبر انسان کی سب سے اہم صفات میں سے ہے۔ یہ بڑی سے بڑی مصیبتوں کو بھی ہلکا کر دیتا ہے، اور اللہ پر توکل کے ساتھ مل کر یہ ایمان کی روح کو بیدار کرتا ہے۔\n\nاسی سورت میں اللہ آزمائشوں کا ذکر کرتے ہوئے فرماتا ہے:\n\n***\"اور ہم ضرور تمہیں خوف، بھوک، مال و جان اور پھلوں کے نقصان سے آزمائیں گے؛ اور صبر کرنے والوں کو خوشخبری سنا دو — جب انہیں کوئی مصیبت پہنچتی ہے تو وہ کہتے ہیں: بے شک ہم اللہ کے ہیں اور اسی کی طرف لوٹنے والے ہیں۔ یہی لوگ ہیں جن پر ان کے رب کی طرف سے رحمت اور عنایات ہیں، اور یہی لوگ ہدایت یافتہ ہیں۔\"***\n(سورۂ بقرہ، آیات ۱۵۵-۱۵۷)\n\nسورۂ آلِ عمران میں اللہ تعالیٰ تین حکم دیتا ہے:\n\n***\"اے ایمان والو! صبر کرو، اور ایک دوسرے کو صبر میں سہارا دو، اور (راہِ خدا میں) ڈٹے رہو؛ اور اللہ سے ڈرتے رہو تاکہ تم فلاح پاؤ۔\"***\n(سورۂ آلِ عمران، آیت ۲۰۰)\n\nعلامہ طباطبائی **المیزان** (جلد ۷، سورۂ آلِ عمران، آیت ۲۰۰) میں اس آیت کی تشریح کرتے ہوئے فرماتے ہیں کہ یہاں تین درجے بیان ہوئے ہیں:\n- **انفرادی صبر** — ہر مشکل میں خود ثابت قدم رہنا\n- **اجتماعی صبر (مصابرت)** — مل کر مشکلات برداشت کرنا، جس سے ہر فرد کا صبر دوگنا ہو جاتا ہے\n- **مرابطت** — راہِ خدا میں ڈٹے رہنا\n\n---\n\n## اہلِ بیت (علیہم السلام) کی تعلیمات میں صبر\n\n### صبر ایمان کا سر ہے\n\nامام جعفر صادق (علیہ السلام) نے فرمایا:\n\n***\"صبر ایمان کا سر ہے۔\"***\n(الکافی، جلد ۲، کتاب ۱، باب ۴۷، حدیث ۱)\n\nامام علی بن الحسین زین العابدین (علیہ السلام) نے اس تشبیہ کو مزید وضاحت سے بیان فرمایا:\n\n***\"صبر کا ایمان سے وہی رشتہ ہے جو سر کا جسم سے ہوتا ہے۔ جس کے پاس صبر نہیں، اس کے پاس ایمان نہیں۔\"***\n(الکافی، جلد ۲، کتاب ۱، باب ۴۷، حدیث ۴)\n\nیعنی جس طرح سر کے بغیر جسم زندہ نہیں رہ سکتا، اسی طرح صبر کے بغیر ایمان کامل نہیں ہو سکتا۔\n\n---\n\n### صبر کی عارضی نوعیت اور اس کا پھل\n\nامام جعفر صادق (علیہ السلام) نے فرمایا:\n\n***\"اے حفص! جو صبر کرتا ہے وہ تھوڑے ہی عرصے کے لیے صبر کرتا ہے، اور جو بے صبری کرتا ہے وہ بھی تھوڑے ہی عرصے کے لیے ایسا کرتا ہے۔ تمام معاملات میں صبر کرو۔\"***\n\nپھر آپ نے یہ آیات تلاوت فرمائیں:\n\n***\"نیکی اور برائی برابر نہیں ہیں؛ برائی کو بھلائی سے دور کرو، تو دیکھو گے کہ جس سے تمہاری دشمنی تھی وہ تمہارا گہرا دوست بن جائے گا — اور یہ مقام صرف انہیں نصیب ہوتا ہے جو صبر کرتے ہیں، اور صرف وہی اس تک پہنچتے ہیں جو بڑے نصیبے والے ہیں۔\"***\n(سورۂ فصلت، آیات ۳۴-۳۵، بحوالہ: الکافی، جلد ۲، کتاب ۱، باب ۴۷، حدیث ۳)\n\n---\n\n### جمیل صبر — شکایت کے بغیر صبر\n\nامام محمد باقر (علیہ السلام) سے پوچھا گیا کہ \"جمیل صبر\" (خوبصورت صبر) کیا ہے؟ آپ نے فرمایا:\n\n***\"وہ صبر جس میں لوگوں کے سامنے کوئی شکایت نہ ہو۔\"***\n(الکافی، جلد ۲، کتاب ۱، باب ۴۷، حدیث ۲۳)\n\nیعنی حقیقی صبر وہ ہے جس میں انسان اللہ کے سوا کسی اور کے سامنے اپنا دکھ نہ رکھے۔\n\n---\n\n### شیعہ کا صبر — ایک منفرد مقام\n\nامام جعفر صادق (علیہ السلام) نے ایک نہایت دلچسپ بات فرمائی:\n\n***\"ہم صبر کرنے میں قوی ہیں، اور ہمارے شیعہ ہم سے بھی زیادہ قوی ہیں۔ میں نے عرض کیا: یا مولا! یہ کیسے؟ فرمایا: ہم ان حقیقتوں کو جانتے ہوئے صبر کرتے ہیں، جبکہ ہمارے شیعہ ایسے معاملات میں صبر کرتے ہیں جن کی حقیقت سے وہ ابھی واقف نہیں۔\"***\n(الکافی، جلد ۲، کتاب ۱، باب ۴۷، حدیث ۲۵)\n\nیہ حدیث مومنین کے صبر کی عظمت کو واضح کرتی ہے — ایمان کی بنیاد پر، بغیر حقیقت کی مکمل جانکاری کے صبر کرنا، ایک بہت اونچا مقام ہے۔\n\n---\n\n## صبر کی اقسام\n\nاہلِ بیت (علیہم السلام) کی تعلیمات اور قرآن کی روشنی میں صبر کی تین اہم اقسام ہیں:\n\n- **مصیبتوں میں صبر** — دکھ، تکلیف اور آزمائش کو اللہ کی رضا سمجھ کر برداشت کرنا\n- **اللہ کی اطاعت میں صبر** — فرائض ادا کرنے میں مستقل رہنا، چاہے مشکل ہو\n- **گناہوں سے بچنے میں صبر** — نفس کی خواہشات کے سامنے ڈٹے رہنا\n\n---\n\n## خلاصہ\n\nصبر محض خاموش برداشت کا نام نہیں، بلکہ یہ ایک فعال، باشعور اور ایمان پر مبنی کیفیت ہے۔ قرآن اسے فلاح کی شرط قرار دیتا ہے، اور اہلِ بیت (علیہم السلام) نے اسے ایمان کی بنیاد فرمایا ہے۔ اللہ تعالیٰ صبر کرنے والوں کے ساتھ ہے — یہ وعدہ خود رب العالمین نے کیا ہے۔\n\n---\n\n## مزید جاننے کے لیے\n\n- صبر اور شکر میں کیا فرق ہے، اور دونوں کا آپس میں کیا تعلق ہے؟\n- امام حسین (علیہ السلام) کی زندگی میں صبر کا کون سا عملی سبق ہے؟\n- مصیبت میں \"انا للہ و انا الیہ راجعون\" کہنے کی روحانی اہمیت کیا ہے؟",
